findings.claim: Removing the try/finally means `this.indent` is never decremented if `fn` throws, leaving the Doc permanently over-indented.
findings.rationale: The deleted comment explicitly documented the invariant: "the compiler catches a child's throw and keeps writing into this doc, so the indent has to unwind with it." If the enclosing compiler catches the exception thrown inside `fn(this)` and continues writing to the same Doc instance (as the comment asserts it does), every subsequent line is emitted at a stale, too-deep indent level, and nested `indented()` calls compound the drift. Unless the throw path was independently proven to always discard the Doc, this is a real behavioral regression; the try/finally cost is negligible here. High confidence this is a bug given the removed comment states the exact scenario.
